---
title: "Primitive API"
description: "Reusable feature, assignment, untreated-outcome, and effect laws."
jupyter: python3
---

```{python}
import inspect

from pypanelsim import primitives

def show(names):
    for name in names:
        value = getattr(primitives, name)
        print(f"{name}{inspect.signature(value)}")
```

## Unit features

```{python}
show((
    "GaussianUnitFeatures",
    "CorrelatedGaussianFeatures",
    "LatentGradientFeatures",
))
```

| Primitive | Use |
|---|---|
| `GaussianUnitFeatures` | independent observed and latent standard-normal features |
| `CorrelatedGaussianFeatures` | observed proxies correlated with latent features |
| `LatentGradientFeatures` | ordered latent position with optional observed proxies |

Feature models return both DGP-visible features and estimator-visible
covariates. These need not be the same matrix.

`att_dml_nonlinear_basis(values)` is a deterministic feature transform used by
the nonlinear conditional-trends design.

## Time features

```{python}
show(("GaussianTimeFeatures",))
```

`n_features` is the number of independent time series. A value of zero returns
an empty time-feature matrix.

## Assignment laws

```{python}
show((
    "SingleCohortAssignment",
    "RandomizedSingleCohortAssignment",
    "StaggeredAdoption",
    "RandomizedStaggeredAdoption",
    "BinaryLogitAssignment",
    "SparseLogitAssignment",
    "GeneralizedPropensityAssignment",
))
```

### Parameter semantics

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n_treated` | number of treated units |
| `adoption_period` | zero-based first treated time position |
| `adoption_periods` | ordered treated-category start positions |
| `cohort_sizes` | sample size for each randomized adoption category |
| `eligible_units` | optional positions from which randomized cohorts are drawn |
| `intercept` or `intercepts` | logit constants |
| `observable_coefficients` | assignment coefficients on observed features |
| `unobservable_coefficients` | assignment coefficients on latent features |

`SingleCohortAssignment` treats the first `n_treated` units unless
`treated_units` is supplied. `StaggeredAdoption` receives an explicit mapping
from unit position to adoption period.

`BinaryLogitAssignment` draws one treated category. `GeneralizedPropensityAssignment`
draws never treated or one of several adoption categories from a multinomial
logit. Coefficient dimensions must match the corresponding feature counts.

## Untreated-outcome laws

```{python}
show((
    "TwoWayFixedEffectsOutcome",
    "AdditiveFactorOutcome",
    "LowRankFactorOutcome",
    "LinearFeatureOutcome",
    "UnitTrendOutcome",
    "UnitPositionOutcome",
    "PeriodicTimeOutcome",
    "ARMAErrorOutcome",
    "RandomARMAErrorOutcome",
    "ClusteredTrendOutcome",
    "LatentSelectionOutcome",
    "SumOutcomeModel",
    "CallableOutcomeModel",
))
```

### Structural guide

| Primitive | Untreated structure |
|---|---|
| `TwoWayFixedEffectsOutcome` | $\alpha_i+\gamma_t+\varepsilon_{it}$ |
| `AdditiveFactorOutcome` | compatibility form of additive unit and time factors |
| `LowRankFactorOutcome` | $\lambda_i'f_t+\varepsilon_{it}$ |
| `LinearFeatureOutcome` | feature-dependent level and linear trend |
| `UnitTrendOutcome` | random or supplied unit-specific slopes |
| `UnitPositionOutcome` | smooth outcome surface over latent unit position |
| `PeriodicTimeOutcome` | shared sine and cosine time terms |
| `ARMAErrorOutcome` | fixed AR and MA coefficients |
| `RandomARMAErrorOutcome` | unit-specific random ARMA coefficients |
| `ClusteredTrendOutcome` | cluster-specific linear trends |
| `LatentSelectionOutcome` | outcome surface linked to latent selection |
| `SumOutcomeModel` | weighted sum of outcome components |
| `CallableOutcomeModel` | adapter for a compatible Python callable |

`LowRankFactorOutcome.rank` is the factor rank. `loading_scale` and
`factor_scale` set factor scales. Separate control and treated loading means can
create limited factor overlap.

`LinearFeatureOutcome.source` is `observables` or `unobservables`.
`level_coefficients` affect the level. `trend_coefficients` multiply the time
index. Set `center_time=True` to center that index.

`SumOutcomeModel` is the main composition tool:

```{python}
combined = primitives.SumOutcomeModel(
    models=(
        primitives.TwoWayFixedEffectsOutcome(noise_scale=0.2),
        primitives.LowRankFactorOutcome(rank=2),
    ),
    weights=(1.0, 0.5),
)
print(combined)
```

## Treatment-effect laws

```{python}
show((
    "ConstantEffect",
    "LinearRampEffect",
    "CohortEventTimeEffect",
    "EventTimeProfileEffect",
    "GaussianCellEffect",
    "RandomUnitEffect",
    "RandomWalkEffect",
    "CallableUnitEffect",
    "CallableEffect",
))
```

| Primitive | Effect surface |
|---|---|
| `ConstantEffect` | same value in every treated cell |
| `LinearRampEffect` | linear in exposure length |
| `CohortEventTimeEffect` | one event-time array for each adoption cohort |
| `EventTimeProfileEffect` | one callable event-time path |
| `GaussianCellEffect` | independent cell heterogeneity around a mean |
| `RandomUnitEffect` | one random effect level per unit |
| `RandomWalkEffect` | stochastic common exposure-time path |
| `CallableUnitEffect` | user callable evaluated by unit and event time |
| `CallableEffect` | adapter for a complete effect-matrix callable |

Every effect model must return realized effects that are zero outside treatment.
It should put the complete `effect_surface` in draw metadata. The simulator
validates `realized = treatment * effect_surface`.

## Profile helpers

```{python}
show((
    "constant_profile",
    "linear_profile",
    "concave_profile",
    "saturating_profile",
    "hump_profile",
    "sinusoidal_profile",
))
```

These functions return deterministic arrays for use with
`CohortEventTimeEffect` or `EventTimeProfileEffect`. They do not assign
treatment and do not include pre-treatment periods.
